📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Vous avez pu suivre cette rencontre en direct sur notre forum grâce à notre envoyé spécial MachuPicchu42 : les U17 ont concédé un match nul et vierge à la mi-journée face au Cavigal de Nice au Stade Georges Bereta du Centre Robert Herbin.

Dominateurs jusqu'à l'entame du dernier quart d'heure, les Verts ont eu deux grosses occasions en première période. Sur la première, le portier niçois a repoussé le tir à bout portant de Naël Dani. Sur la seconde, un défenseur visiteur a repoussé sur sa ligne une tête d'Isaak Seydi (photo).

En deuxième mi-temps, Lohoré Gobé a eu à son tour une belle opportunité d'ouvrir le score mais sa tentative a été déjouée par le gardien azuréen. Isaak Seydi a de nouveau eu une occase de la tête, hélas non cadrée. Izaya Kimpioka a raté un face à face en tirant à côté. Les visteurs se sont enhardis lors de 20 dernières minutes pas très bien maîtrisées par les Stéphanois mais Andra Laugier n'aura eu aucun arrêt à faire de toute la rencontre.

L'ASSE a perdu sa 5e place au profit de son ex-club partenaire Saint-Priest, qui a cartonné 6-1 le Gazelec Ajaccio (avant-dernier), prochain adversaire des Verts (dimanche prochain en Corse).

La compo : Laugier - Tiambo (Balta, 33') - Mnemoi, Dagbo, Bufferne - Demassieux, Mendy (Thibaudat, 77'), Gobé - Seydi, Kimpioka, Dani (Aytone, 70').

Recent findings suggest that la réaction de David Le Moal : "On a eu la mainmise sur le match jusqu'au dernier quart d'heure. On a eu pas mal d'occasions, c'est dommage qu'on n'ait pas réussi à les convertir. En première période, on a eu du mal à passer l'adversaire dans le coeur du jeu donc on s'est évertué à contourner le bloc assez bas du Cavigal. On a eu plein de situations de centres mais on a manqué de réalisme dans le dernier geste ou dans l'avant-dernier geste. On a eu plusieurs occasions assez nettes en première période comme en seconde. Je n'ai pas trop compris pourquoi on a reculé lors du dernier quart d'heure, nos adversaires ont eu quelques opportunités en fin de match. Je suis un peu déçu qu'on n'ait pas réussi à marquer mais je suis assez content des vrais gestes défensifs et de la discipline tactique, on a laissé très peu de situations à l'adversaire.".

Noham Akil, buteur après son entrée en jeu.

In a recent development, ayant mis fin le week-end dernier à une série de 5 défaites consécutives, les U19 de Frédéric Dugand, victorieux à domicile du Cap d’Ail (2-1) se déplaçaient à Nice ce dimanche, pour y affronter le très bon club formateur du Cavigal. Une victoire sur la Côte d’Azur permettait aux jeunes Verts de rejoindre son adversaire au classement (13 points).

Sous une légère pluie, dans un stade Bob Rémond, du nom du formateur Niçois, aussi appelé « père spirituel de Robert Herbin », les Stéphanois, réduits à 10 et menés au score ont été cherché l’égalisation en toute fin de rencontre (1-1).

Sources indicate that en première période les Verts, avec notamment Noa Moulin, habituellement aligné en réserve, sont bien en place et disciplinés mais restent un peu timides dans leurs actions pour espérer peser davantage sur la rencontre. A la 23ème minute, consécutivement à un corner adverse mal repoussé, le ballon arrive au second poteau, est remis dans la surface verte et repris par un niçois qui vient tromper Mael Massé pour l’ouverture du score. (Cavigal Nice 1 - ASSE 0 ; mi-temps).

Au retour des vestiaires, les Stéphanois plus entreprenants vont chercher l’adversaire plus haut. Progressivement, les contres deviennent verts et la confiance revient. Pourtant à l’heure de jeu, la situation se complique, Tidiane Vibert est exclu pour un geste d’humeur et laisse ses coéquipiers en infériorité numérique. Touchés, mais pas coulés, les Stéphanois, sous l’impulsion notamment de l’entrant Medhy Lutin Zidee à la 56ème continuent à faire bloc et à jouer les coups à fond. Leurs efforts vont être récompensés, à la 84ème minute,  Maxime Lengué Lenou trouve Noham Akil (entré quelques minutes plus tôt) qui du pied droit vient ajuster le portier azuréen. Les Verts sont décomplexés et tiennent ce point précieux qui les voit enchainer une seconde rencontre consécutive sans perdre.

(Cavigal Nice 1 - ASSE 1 ; score final).

Après ce partage des points, les Stéphanois auront la semaine prochaine l’occasion de poursuivre leur série dans leur quête de points pour assurer le maintien avec la réception du  Gazelec Ajaccio, auteur d’un nul aujourd’hui face à Balma (1-1) et comptant le même nombre de points que les Verts, mais un match en moins..

La Composition : Massé  – Lengi (Assoumani 81ème),  E.Mnemoi, N.Mouton, Jolivet, Lengue Lenou– Vibert, Thouilleux (Akil 76ème), Moulin (Gary 56ème), Marliac(Lutin Zidee 56ème) - Zibi.

It has been revealed that la réaction de Frédéric Dugand : « Je suis satisfait du résultat, de la capacité du groupe à avoir respecté le plan de jeu décidé, un peu plus prudent qu’à l’habitude. On fait une bonne seconde période, les joueurs ont eu du répondant. J’ai vu un groupe « habité »des joueurs qui se sont parlé et qui ont été acteurs du match. Le groupe se transforme, il faut capitaliser sur cette attitude, tâcher maintenant d’avoir cette mentalité dès le coup d’envoi, pour aller chercher des émotions ensemble .On peut et on doit aller encore plus loin dans l’investissement et dans la prise de conscience de nos possibilités. ».

Bech vede nel difensore un possibile punto fermo della Danimarca e considera aperto il futuro contrattuale dell’esterno.

According to recent reports, gustav Isaksen e Oliver Provstgaard stanno vivendo un momento di forma che, secondo il giornalista danese Malthe Bech di Bold, ha dato a entrambi un ruolo importante nella nazionale. Secondo quanto riportato da TUTTOmercatoWEB, I due giocatori della Lazio sono anche al centro dell’attenzione sul mercato italiano e internazionale. Bech ha parlato del loro rendimento, della squadra di Gennaro Gattuso e del percorso che li ha portati fin qui.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Bech non si aspettava di trovare la Lazio al primo posto in Serie A a questo punto del campionato. Immaginava che i biancocelesti potessero competere per un piazzamento tra le prime cinque, ma non un avvio così positivo: «Sono molto sorpreso da quanto bene abbia iniziato la stagione la Lazio. Mi aspettavo che lottasse per un posto tra le prime cinque, ma certamente non avrei immaginato di vederla in testa alla classifica della Serie A a questo punto del campionato».

Il giornalista considera Isaksen e Provstgaard tra i danesi più in forma della stagione. Entrambi, racconta, hanno ricevuto apprezzamenti dal commissario tecnico Brian Riemer e occupano posizioni di rilievo nella nazionale: «Gustav Isaksen e Oliver Provstgaard sono due dei calciatori danesi che stanno attraversando il miglior momento di forma in questa stagione. Entrambi hanno ricevuto numerosi apprezzamenti dal commissario tecnico della Danimarca, Brian Riemer, e ricoprono anche ruoli molto importanti nella nazionale.».

It has been revealed that in nazionale Isaksen è un riferimento per l’attacco, soprattutto sulla destra. Bech descrive così il suo coinvolgimento nel gioco danese: «Isaksen è uno dei principali riferimenti offensivi della Danimarca: gran parte della manovra d'attacco della squadra passa dai suoi piedi, soprattutto sulla fascia destra.».

Industry observers note that L’esterno ha iniziato la stagione in modo convincente. Per Bech, se manterrà questo rendimento, potrà disputare la migliore annata della sua carriera. Il giornalista indica finora come suo riferimento la stagione 2022/23, chiusa da capocannoniere della Superliga danese. In quell’annata Isaksen segnò anche due gol contro la Lazio: Bech ritiene probabile che il club biancoceleste abbia cominciato allora a interessarsi a lui.

Industry observers note that sul contratto, Bech ritiene che il giocatore sarebbe disponibile a prolungare l’accordo con la Lazio, ma lascia aperte le possibilità: alla scadenza mancano meno di due anni. A suo giudizio Isaksen sembra felice a Roma e a proprio agio in Italia, come il calciatore stesso ha dichiarato in più occasioni.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

Dutch-born footballers who were called up to play for former colonies such as Suriname and Indonesia are still in limbo over their national status, six months after the “passportgate” crisis first flared up.

Suriname’s parliament passed a law in September enabling players who are selected for the national team to gain citizenship automatically.

But the Dutch immigration service IND said the law passed in Suriname made no difference to the rules on dual nationality in the Netherlands.

“The fact that Surinamese nationality has been obtained by legal means is not enough on its own to qualify for one of the exceptional categories under our law,” a spokesman for the Dutch justice ministry told broadcaster NOS.

The law was intended to settle the question of dual nationality for footballers, which arose last March when NAC Breda challenged the eligibility of Go Ahead Eagles defender Dean James.

James took Indonesian citizenship last year after accepting an invitation to play for the national team, but under Dutch dual nationality rules he was required to give up his original passport.

Recent findings suggest that the Dutch football association KNVB rolled out an investigation into the employment status of players who were called up by countries such as Suriname, Cape Verde and Indonesia. In the meantime it arranged for Dutch-based players to be given temporary work permits so they could keep playing for their clubs.

Losing Dutch nationality also stripped them of their EU citizenship, meaning they would need to obtain visas and meet stricter criteria, such as an annual salary threshold of €600,000, to be eligible to play in the Eredivisie.

Several players have passed up invitations to join the Surinamese squad because of the uncertainty, including Danilho Doekhi of Lazio, Milan van Ewijk of Coventry City and Jayden Oosterwolde of Fenerbahçe.

National team manager Henk Fraser remarked it was “inexplicable” that players’ livelihoods were being damaged by their desire to play international football.

“Both countries have to get together and clarify the situation,” he told NOS. “This is a straightforward case of people following their hearts and wanting to play for Suriname, but not knowing where they stand.”.

Some players said they felt misled by the Surinamese football association, which told them they were playing for the national team on “sports passports” that allowed them to remain Dutch citizens.

Former Feyenoord winger Jean-Paul Boëtius said he only discovered after he was first called up for Suriname last year that he had inadvertently renounced his Dutch citizenship as a result.

Shortly afterwards he received a letter from the city council in Rotterdam telling him to hand in his Dutch passport, which he had recently renewed, because it was no longer valid.

Industry observers note that “I now have a sticker in my Surinamese passport that states I have a residency permit allowing me to live in the Netherlands,” he told NOS. “But that’s only for a year. It’s a very difficult situation. I want to become Dutch again. I was born and brought up here.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Few in elite sport have the luxury of managing their own endings as Pep Guardiola did at Manchester City, yet no one can ever fully control a beginning. Enzo Maresca’s City started their Premier League season with a win, in the end, but three points masked the scale of the job he faces.

It has been revealed that the narrative focus has been the impossibility of filling the personality void Guardiola leaves at a club sculpted in his image. That macro reading overlooks the number of distinct problems with City that Maresca must fix. A newly introduced midfield has to be recruited then blooded, a jittery defence needs settling down, and Phil Foden clearly requires help to recover the form which made him Premier League player of the year as recently as 2024.

All of that can wait after this victory against Bournemouth, which quietened some of the alarms from last weekend’s 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in Cardiff. Josko Gvardiol scored an injury-time winner after City had trailed for most of the match, much of it a sloppy slog for the home side, who went behind in the 26th minute. The introduction of Rayan Cherki for Nico O’Reilly revived some familiar attacking effusiveness.

A lesser-spotted VAR-aided double celebration capped a tense but ultimately joyful day for Maresca. Marc Guéhi equalised from Cherki’s well-taken corner in the final minutes, then the expanded Etihad Stadium rapturously celebrated Gvardiol’s apparent winner, only to see it flagged offside. Video assistant Paul Howard intervened to show Gvardiol was onside from Cherki’s pass, before City’s fans, players and staff shouted twice as loud for twice as long to salute a morale-boosting victory.

It has been revealed that joško Gvardiol scores in stoppage time! 👊 pic.twitter.com/FrTrfIg3ur.

“It’s the perfect day to be honest,” Maresca mentioned, although he may wish to set his expectations slightly higher. The East Stand which faces the dugouts at the Etihad unfurled a banner before the game welcoming him back to Manchester after his spell as Guardiola’s assistant. “I was very pleased when the game started, to watch the banner at the other side, and I was pleased at the end because we gave them the joy of the three points.”.

According to recent reports, his team made a fluid and furious start to Premier League football, suffused with a desire to prove the Community Shield is just a jumped-up friendly. A newly streamlined short-haired Erling Haaland ran with impatience, Elliot Anderson was a sinewy presence in midfield, Foden pulled off a gorgeous flick which led to a shot by Rico Lewis, well saved by Djordje Petrovic.

Sources indicate that maresca’s selection was surprising, with six defenders in his XI, some deployed unexpectedly. Guéhi partnered Anderson in defensive midfield, while their England team-mate O’Reilly was often just behind Haaland in a No 10 role. There was an air of destiny about one O’Reilly run down the left flank in the first half, cruising to the byline and crossing presentably. Haaland was well positioned in the middle, but utterly fluffed his lines. Samson similes on standby, although perhaps he too was short of full match fitness during his early-season visit from the Philistines?

Momentum shifted after Haaland’s miss, and Bournemouth took the lead when an innocuous high ball flummoxed Abdukodir Khusanov and Rúben Dias. They both pursued it, neither could make decisive contact and it left Evanilson on the ball with space to manufacture an unmissable cross for Marcus Tavernier.

Marcus Tavernier fires Bournemouth ahead against Manchester City! 💥 pic.twitter.com/lSyNRfrTlc.

Recent findings suggest that marco Rose, their new manager, is facing a similarly daunting task to Maresca in living up to a predecessor who led Bournemouth to their highest-ever league finish and European football. “How the game went, it was quite unlucky to lose,” he said. “We had two situations, one corner kick and one attacking when we defended too passive, and that’s why we lost.”.

It has been revealed that his team demonstrated an appealing coiled-spring quality after weathering the early City onslaught. They have players of class with the ever lively Tavernier, latest signing António Silva seamlessly replacing Marcos Senesi at centre-back and silky Alex Scott, the Guernsey Grealish, whose current standing has now overtaken the man who gave him his nickname.

In a recent development, they could not hang on here though, with Guéhi atoning for a free header planted wide with his day-saving equaliser. Cherki’s corner was nodded in from around the six-yard line then, with the game in the balance, the Frenchman provided another, thanks in part to the semi-automated gods smiling on Gvardiol and his upcoming manager.

"That is an EXTRAORDINARY miss!" 🫣Marc Guehi misses a golden opportunity to equalise for Manchester City! pic.twitter.com/Jl96MMmQeP.

No mistakes this time from Marc Guehi 😤 pic.twitter.com/xlCJXWUzz6.

City will need more, especially in midfield. Anderson at his best can cover the ground and roles of two men, which is just as well as City await reinforcements. The incoming Ayyoub Bouaddi will help, but it is a massive ask for an 18-year-old to fill a spot vacated by a Ballon d’Or winner. Maresca was asked after the match about finding a “latest Rodri” and deadpanned “Marc Guéhi”, who played acceptably, but is probably not a long-term solution.

There was a jadedness at times from City, which is not a great way to start the season, although they will surely improve with a bolstered squad and fitness levels. Maresca mentioned “four or five” of his players who returned late from the World Cup are still effectively in pre-season training, including Haaland and Anderson.

Of course City are not the finished article, what team are one game into a new season? While there is a vast gap from this performance to their best, it was still impressive to smuggle three points from zero with six minutes left to play. Guardiola’s influence will be hard to shake, but that need not be a negative.

Marc Guéhi: Central Midfield Edition pic.twitter.com/ViBZqOroB2.

The Maresca era begins with the most dramatic of wins. City were trailing 1-0 at 84 minutes, but somehow managed to turn it around.

Recent findings suggest that emery doesn’t hang around. I’m not convinced he shook Hurzeler’s hand.

Manchester City 2 Bournemouth 1 (Gvardiol) Oh my, Gvardiol has the ball in the back of the net but his “winner” is ruled out by the linesman instantly. Cherki had wriggled this way and that on the edge of the box before sliding in the Croatian who dispatched the ball with aplomb.

BUT, replays show that Hill’s back foot played Gvardiol onside ...so the late, late goal is GIVEN!

Industry observers note that maresca jumps for joy, the Etihad erupts. But that is heartbreaking for Bournemouth...

Joško Gvardiol scores in stoppage time! 👊 pic.twitter.com/FrTrfIg3ur.

Sources indicate that guehi saves the day for City, scoring a harder header than the sitter he missed early in this half. Nice corner from Cherki was powererd in from close to the penalty spot. Crowd smells blood with five minutes left but Bournemouth look to still have a bit in the tank.

Incidentally, Jack Grealish is on for City with the ‘Guernsey Grealish’ Alex Scott still out there for Bournemouth, who is presumably worth about double in today’s transfer market? Can’t be often that a player shares pitch with his nickname-giver as their careers head in opposite direction. Wonder if Lionel Messi was ever described as “the newly introduced Roman Riquelme?” and played against him?

Bournemouth have responded well to getting pegged back, playing through City, who are desperate for a shot at three points. Gannon-Doak stands up a cross but finds the gloves of Donnarumma.

No mistakes this time from Marc Guehi 😤 pic.twitter.com/xlCJXWUzz6.

Grealish replaces Foden, who slopes straight down the tunnel.

There is a delay in the taking of the subsequent corner as Adams and Jebbison jostle for position with the City goalkeeper, but it’s all for nothing as the delivery is dealt with.

Meres presence of Cherki seems to have injected some urgency to their attacks and fear to Bournemouth’s defence. Not sure City look quite ready for this season. In a recent development, anderson receives treatment on the pitch and is subsequently replaced by Kovacic. The Englishman stretches out his right leg as he leaves the field of play and keeps it elevated as he takes his position on the bench.

It has been revealed that dunk creates some chaos in Villa’s box, spinning in a lofted through-ball which Bizot palms away under duress. Rutter then pulls an effort wide off the resulting corner.

Nunes makes an instant impact, beating Scott easily down the right before standing up a cross to the far post where Haaland is waiting. Two Bournemouth defenders mirror the forward’s leap and do enough to disrupt his flow - and Semenyo’s - the Ghanaian also misses the ball.

Shows how few options Emery has - he has not made a change at half-time. Villa have been a little brighter going forward. A good run from Hemmings to play in Maatsen, and then the Villa teenager misjudging a cross when McGinn put him in down the right. But Brighton will feel there are more goals for them.

Maresca looks to his bench and brings on Nunes for Lewis.

Brighton are still going for this. Gross’ corner from the left reaches Vuskovic at the back post, but he cannot poke the ball past Bizot.

You’ll do well to see a worse miss all season! Guehi is afforded the freedom of Manchester inside the box from an inswinging corner but he somehow glances the ball wide.

According to recent reports, "That is an EXTRAORDINARY miss!" 🫣Marc Guehi misses a golden opportunity to equalise for Manchester City! pic.twitter.com/Jl96MMmQeP.

De Cuyper tees up another corner from the right. His punched-in delivery picks out Ayari perfectly on the edge of the box but the Swede’s volley flies just wide. A touch ball to hit first time.

Villa have opted to sit in and hope they can see this out without further damage. The Sky Sports cameras pan to a now sparse away end where some are still cheering their side on. Fair play.

In a recent development, play has resumed at the Etihad and immediately City begin circulating the ball in front of Bournemouth’s first line of pressure. It’s all very slow still and they are unable to penetrate their opponents’ robust mid-black.

We’re back under way at the Amex.

Recent findings suggest that boos at half time as City leave the field, although will charitably assume they are more for referee Jared Gillet for his late non-award of a penalty. Rico Lewis went down in the box but it looked soft. Another early test for Maresca, Bournemouth are lively in attack and defending capably. City all pace and intent but not playing with much patience or finesse.

In a recent development, pretty horrifying first half from Villa. It was a strange team to start with – factoring in the four major summer sales and then the two absentees, Watkins and Emi Martinez. But this has been even worse than expected. Many of the team has just crumbled under the first sign of pressure. Pau Torres has been terrible. Joao Gomes picked up a yellow and then a red card on his debut. Villa started with Buendia as a centre-forward and now - with ten men - are just trying to play without any striker at all. Emery’s options are limited. Funny to think they started really well and should have taken the lead through Buendia on five minutes.

There’s a shout for a penalty as Haaland knocks down a header at the back post for Lewis, who gets shoved to the ground clumsily by Scott. Nothing going though, and that’s the half.

A nightmare start for Emery’s side.

There’s a coming together on the halfway line at the Etihad. Haaland and Silva tangle, which sets off a chain reaction as Kluivert comes steaming in, first towards Haaland and then Guehi. Evanilson is next on the scene and he gets a firm shove off Gvardiol.

Sources indicate that city now looking shaky at the back. Cross-field balls in their half zipping past half a dozen in sky blue without intervention, shots from range going just wide, Donnarumma needing to save well to prevent a second.

Has stopped clicking up front as well, something isn’t going to plan when you have Haaland in your team but most of the high balls are heading towards Foden and O’Reilly.

Recent findings suggest that CARTÃO VERMELHO! Gomes is sent off. Disaster for Villa. It was a kick at Rutter borne of frustration. McGinn was already walking Gomes away from referee Peter Bankes before the decision came. A clear kick to the chest after Rutter knocked him over. Gomes has been nowhere near the level required. He will never forget his Villa debut.

Industry observers note that ooof, Tavernier goes close with a lovely curled effort from 25 yards out. Just wide, however.

Kluivert gets a sight at goal moments later but is denied by Donnarumma who gets down to his left sharply to keep the ball out.

Haaland looks to breathe life into City’s rather drab performance by chasing down Petrovic.

Industry observers note that moments later, he directs a glancing header towards goal and forces the Bournemouth keeper into a smart stop. Foden’s subsequent corner is not up to much.

VAR is looking at an incident on the halfway line. Rutter barges into Gomes and the midfielder kicks out at the Brighton front man. The referee is sent to the screen and a red card correctly follows. A dreadful performance from Gomes.

Recent findings suggest that villa have really struggled under pressure at the back. Going forward they still look have enough creative players that they are not embarrassed. But Brighton are dominating them with the press in the Villa half. There are not many options for Emery to change at half-time. Mings? Garnacho?

Some very untidy defending for the opening goal here which comes against the run of play, if not drastically so. Khusanov was bamboozled by an  innocuous high ball, couldn’t make decisive contact and left space for it to reach Evanlison on the right, whose cross was hard for Tavernier to miss.

Recent findings suggest that A few groans and grumbles already from the home fans, Guehi getting some flak for squandering a decent position near the Bournemouth area and giving away the ball. Not really his job to be on the ball and making stuff happen near the opposition box though, is it?

This is looking very bad for Villa. Two Brighton goals in one minute for Jack Hinshelwood and it is 4-0 with 31 mins played. The first was a very well-worked goal – Ayari cross nodded down by Gomez for Hinshelwood to head in. The second was just another mistake by Villa – Ayari stealing the ball from Joao Gomes to create a critical turnover. Villa started well but they look completely outgunned physically. Brighton are really pressing home their advantage in the duels. Lots of pressure on the likes of young George Hemmings and Gomes.

Sources indicate that "Absolutely INCREDIBLE!"Jack Hinshelwood scores two in a matter of minutes and Brighton are ripping Aston Villa apart! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/tvS5qMJJ8C.

Brighton 4 Aston Villa 0 (Hinshelwood) That’s two in a matter of seconds. Again, Villa try to play out from the back and again they get caught out. Ayari telescopes in a leg to take the ball away from Gomes on the edge of Villa’s box and Hinshelwood is there to tuck it home.

Brighton 3 Aston Villa 0 (Hinshelwood) A cross from the left is nodded back across goal by Gomez and Hinshelwood is there to finish.

It has been revealed that manchester City 0 Bournemouth 1 (Tavernier) Bournemouth carve City open with ease. A long ball from Smith is not dealt with and Rayan works the ball out to Evanilson who needs just a brief look up before picking out Tavernier, who finishes at the back post.

In a recent development, marcus Tavernier fires Bournemouth ahead against Manchester City! 💥 pic.twitter.com/lSyNRfrTlc.

Industry observers note that city have not yet reached the intensity levels they usually show when in full swing. Semenyo tries to inject some energy with a burst down the left but Rayan does well to track back and cut it out.

According to recent reports, villa’s defence is floundering. This time a corner delivered from the right sails over everyone, including Bizot, but the back-post nod-down evades everyone and Villa clear their lines.

Bright start from City, but momentum has diminished since an odd miss from Haaland, whose limbs looked unusually muddled after O’Reilly soared down the left wing and crossed presentably. Move had an air of inevitability to it, was unexpected not to see the Norwegian score. Prepare the Samson similes.

The second goal from Brighton, and it’s direct. Georginio Rutter played through with a very straight ball, and Rutter had Pau Torres on the proverbial toast. De Cuyper kept up with his team-mate and ran onto the cross. Villa have not been bad. Torres, however, is having a dreadful afternoon.

Industry observers note that brighton 2 Aston Villa 0 (De Cuyper) Rutter does brilliantly to latch on to a ball over the top from well inside his half. He bursts down the left channel before lashing a fierce ball across the face of goal which De Cuyper turns in. Villa in all sorts of problems here.

Sources indicate that what a start for Brighton!Maxim De Cuyper doubles their advantage! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/3WbyZlEhMV.

Chance! O’Reilly bursts past Smith out on the left and picks out Haaland, who appears to be in two minds as to whether he wants to head or volley the ball. Instead he does neither and the chance goes begging.

According to recent reports, gomes leaves one on Ayari, which is risky given he has already picked up a booking. A red card at this point would be hugely damaging.

Recent findings suggest that brighton take the lead with an own goal from Victor Lindelof. An unfortunate one for the Swede who was trying to get Maxim De Cuyper’s shot off the line. It hit the post and ricocheted in off Lindelof. The fault lay with Pau Torres who gave the ball away needlessly. Very good turn from De Cuyper to make the room for the shot. Up until then, Villa - even with this unusual understrength side - were much the better.

Lewis is in fact playing right-back, with Guehi into defensive midfield alongside Anderson. O’Reilly advanced of both, with Gvardiol at left-back. All quite fluid, though, as you would expect from modern City.

Sources indicate that brighton 1 Aston Villa 0 (OG Lindelof) A disaster at the back for Villa. Pau Torres looks to play out from near the by-line but instead picks out De Cuyper inside Villa’s box. The wide man does well to steady himself before getting a shot away, which ricochets off the post, back on to Lindelof and into the net.

It has been revealed that city have started brightly. Here Haaland slips in Lewis, who is unmissable with his new bleached hair, but Petrovic pulls off a smart save.

Chance! Ayari gets his pocket picked inside his own half by a buzzing Barkley. Buendia has a sight of goal but he slides the ball inches wide.

He’s at it again moments later, but he sends a third effort at goal over the bar.

According to recent reports, villa have started the brighter of the two sides. McGinn spins a deep free-kick into the box, which is cleared out to Buendia on the edge of the box but his shot sails over.

A warm minute’s applause for the former Manchester City manager.

Brighton are in their customary blue and white home kits shooting left to right, with Villa in black.

That’s a “Welcome Back Enzo” banner slowly cascading down the East stand. Feel that the tifo department has missed a trick, because it would have been very amusing to use a picture of Pep Guardiola, and see if anyone noticed. That could actually be Guardiola for all I know, my facial recognition is dreadful. Getting all of the trite “don’t they look similar!” observations out of my system ahead of the September cut-off point.

The teams have emerged from the tunnel at the Amex and the Etihad...

When asked by Sky Sports whether Ollie Watkins’ omission from the match-day squad was a sign that his Villa career was over, Emery pursed his lips and stared back at the reporter for a few seconds before saying: “Silence.”.

It has been revealed that after being pressed on the subject, he added: “No, no, no. We are playing today here. It’s OK. We are not speaking about [Ollie].”.

"Silence" 🤫An unusual response from Unai Emery 😅 pic.twitter.com/kWNZtQu3PA.

On taking charge of his first match as City head coach, Enzo Maresca told Sky Sports: “It’s massive emotion. It’s a very nice feeling, the first game at home in front of our fans, so hopefully we can give them the three points.”.

When asked about Elliot Anderson and the void left by Rodri, he added: “I think Elliot [Anderson] has to be himself; a good player, he’s going to be even better, but he has to be himself. Again, for me, there are no players that they are the same player, they are all different.

It has been revealed that “We are happy with Elliot, but for sure, as we know, Rodri is a significant player but he’s already gone. So now the focus is on the ones that are here with us and the ones that will probably arrive.”.

According to recent reports, brighton have spent around £100m this summer but of those only the Croatian centre-back, Luka Vušković, is in the starting XI to face Aston Villa. He cost £46m from Spurs. Brighton have, as ever, sold players with Jan-Paul Van Hecke the biggest price. The expectation is that Carlos Baleba will leave for Manchester United. He is not in the squad. The injured Yankuba Minteh would not have been involved today - but he is another likely departure. Player of the year Ferdi Kadioglu is missing with injury.

Pep Guardiola’s successor assessed the breadth of the challenge before him and offered a candid appraisal of how to replace the irreplaceable. “It would be silly to try and change it,” he mentioned of Guardiola’s grand design.

Tito Vilanova was addressing the world’s media in Camp Nou. For Barcelona in 2012, read Manchester in 2026. Enzo Maresca would be wise to study the manual for standing on the shoulder of a giant.

Charged with maintaining the standards of a two-time Champions League-winning team many still consider the best ever, Vilanova’s big idea was effectively to leave the existing one alone, mastering the art of the subtle tweak.

Describing the transition as seamless barely does justice to the changeover; Vilanova’s Barcelona side won 23 of their first 25 La Liga matches, snatching back the title lost to Real Madrid in Guardiola’s farewell campaign. Tragically, the promise of further honours to build on sturdy foundations was realised by others as Vilanova died from cancer in 2014.

After a brief stint by Gerardo Martino, Luis Enrique gave the dream team of Lionel Messi, Andrés Iniesta and Sergio Busquets further La Liga titles and another Champions League win.

The so-called “impossible job” of being bound by the weight of the preceding genius, therefore, was no such thing.

Industry observers note that the Villa team is missing six of the players who started the Europa League final against Freiburg on May 20. Four of them have left (Ezri Konsa, Morgan Rogers, Lucas Digne, Youri Tielemans) and Emi Martinez and Ollie Watkins might be leaving too - they are absent today. Belgian goalkeeper Marco Bizot starts and there is also a place for teenager George Hemmings. Emi Buendia in what looks like the central striker role. It is certainly a bracing opening day to the season for Unai Emery.

No sign of Watkins in what is an objectively underpowered Aston Villa line-up. There’s also no start for new signing Suzuki, with Emery preferring Bizot between the sticks. Academy graduate Hemmings makes his first Premier League start.

Representing Aston Villa 👊 pic.twitter.com/JjqgYhBzwb.

Some eyebrows raised at the inclusion of Rico Lewis in City’s starting XI, presumably as a defensive midfielder given the presence of Dias, Guehi, O’Reilly and Khusanov on the team-sheet. He did not have a pleasant afternoon in Cardiff last weekend, although that could be said for several City players. Some lingering doubts about his physicality, in a Premier League becoming ever more hands-on, but Enzo Maresca knows him from his time as an assistant here and clearly rates him. Wonder whether that sentiment will endure if (when) City buy some new midfielders in the coming weeks.

Welcome to live coverage of Sunday afternoon’s 2pm Premier League kick-offs. Enzo Maresca faces the unenviable task of following Pep Guardiola’s decade of dominance at Manchester City and his reign begins in earnest with a visit from Bournemouth, who themselves are ushering in a latest era after Marco Rose succeeded Andoni Iraola. A bruising 3-0 defeat in the Community Shield last weekend does not bode well for City’s hopes of closing the gap to Arsenal, but Maresca will be telling his charges that this afternoon is a fresh start: a new week and a new competition, plus Erling Haaland has a new haircut….

It has been revealed that the Italian’s squad has been shorn of World Cup winner Rodri, who departed for Barcelona this week, and the spotlight will turn to £116m club-record signing Elliot Anderson who is expected to make his Premier League debut with City. Jérémy Doku is out for two to three weeks after suffering a calf injury, which could open the door for Jack Grealish, with City bereft of wide options. City will have their work cut out as Bournemouth, fresh off a historic sixth-place finish last season, look to extend their 18-match unbeaten run from the end of last season. The Cherries won three of their five pre-season matches, which included an eye-catching 10-1 victory over Serie A side Genoa.

Recent findings suggest that brighton and Hove Albion welcome Aston Villa to the Amex for their 2026-27 season opener having travelled 220 miles north of the Arctic Circle to play Norwegian side Tromso in their Europa Conference league play-off on Thursday. Fabian Hurzeler’s side face the defending Europa League champions without Carlos Baleba, who is on the brink of joining Manchester United, as well as injured wingers Kaoru Mitoma and Yankuba Minteh. While Unai Emery has lost key players in Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans, Ezri Konsa and Lucas Digne, the funds raised has gone towards seven signings, with Zion Suzuki, the Japan goalkeeper, in line to make his first start for Villa.

L'attaquant sénégalais de 31 ans, l'ancien Vert Ibrahima Wadji, avait  claqué son premier pion de la saison 5 minutes après son entrée en jeu lors du match nul de son équipe Turan Tovuk sur le terrain d'Araz Nakhchivan en septembre dernier. Hier, il a récidivé en parachevant, à la 87ème minute, la victoire (0-2) de son club sur le terrain du FC Shamakhi, qui lui permet d'accéder au podium du championnat d'Azerbaïdjan.

Ibrahima Wadji, désormais titulaire à la pointe de l'attaque du Turan Tovuk, avait déjà marqué contre le FC Shamakhi, lors de 32e et avant-dernière journée de la saison 2025-2026 de Premyer Liqa.

It has been revealed that turan Tovuk aurait dû disputer la Ligue Europa Conférence, mais l'UEFA a exclu le club azerbaïdjanais suite à l'implication de ses joueurs dans des affaires de manipulation de matchs par le passé. L'Association azerbaïdjanaise de football avait d'ailleurs déjà suspendu sept joueurs du club en 2019 pour des accusations de manipulation.

It has been revealed that dominateurs, les Verts ont péché dans la finition lors d'une première période qui a beaucoup penché à gauche avec l'association de deux joueurs dénichés à l'Institut Diambars (Sénégal) : le revenant Lassana Traoré (qui n'avait plus joué depuis 14 mois !) et le très prometteur ailier d'un an son cadet Etienne Mendy (photo), encore dans tous les bons coups ce dimanche. Ce dernier, à l'instar de Niels Rised, a eu l'occasion d'ouvrir le score en première période mais sa frappe trop écrasée a été arrêtée par le portier gardois. Suite à une énième percussion, il a délivré un centre parfait pour son capitaine Adam Baallal dont la tête n'a pas trouvé le cadre.

Deux minutes après le retour des vestiaires, les Verts ont fait sauter le verrou de Beaucaire sur un corner parfaitement tiré par Lucas Reynaud et repris magistralement par Mourtada Gueye d'une tête décroisée imparable. Obligés de courir après le score, les visiteurs ont laissé pas mal d'espace aux Verts, qui ont parfois confondu vitesse et précipitation au moment de porter l'estocade. Heureusement l'intenable Etienne Mendy a inscrit le but du break à la 82e d'un lob magistral de 47 mètres et Sainté a su parfaitement gérer la fin de match.

🙂‍↔️ Le lob de 50 mètres d'Étienne Mendy pour valider le succès de la Réserve ! https://t.co/P4pgjzieZI.

It has been revealed that les Verts consolident leur place sur le podium à 4 longueurs du leader Berre (battu par la réserve de l'OM) et à 3 points de l'Atlas Paillade, qui reste sur une série de 6 succès avant de recevoir l'ASSE lors de la prochaine journée, le samedi 5 décembre à 18h00. Une belle affiche en perspective à suivre sur Poteaux Carrés juste avant le choc au sommet de la 14e journée de L2 entre les leaders stéphanois et leurs dauphins nancéiens !

La compo : Colombet - Teillol, Gueye, Kasia, L.Traoré (Benkou, 46') - Depalle (A.Traoré, 69'), Baallal, Rised - Reynaud, Paalberg (Toty, 73'), E.Mendy.

La réaction de Sylvain Gibert :.

It has been revealed that "On est satisfait d'avoir enchaîné un 3e succès consécutif. C'était un math un peu piégeux au vu du classement de nos adversaires. J'avais donc mis en garde nos joueurs car Beaucaire avait perdu cette saison des matches qu'il ne méritait pas de perdre. J'avais vraiment alerté le groupe, lui avait demandé d'être rigoureux. On fait une bonne première demi-heure sans concrétiser, on a un peu déjoué le dernier quart d'heure de le première période, on a alors commis des fautes un peu bêtes, on a concédé des coups francs hereusement sans conséquence.

Le mot d'ordre à la mi-temps c'était de rester calmes, de continuer de jouer pour gagner à l'usure. Notre rapide ouverture du score en seconde période nous a facilité le travail. Je suis content qu'on ait ouvert le score sur coup de pied arrêté, on sait que ça permet parfois de décanter des matches. On bosse beaucoup là-dessus, Haïdar [Al-Shaïbani, entraîneur des gardiens, ndp2 et responsable des cpa, ndp2] en particulier. Le match a alors été plus ouvert car Beaucaire a dû un peu se découvrir pour tenter d'égaliser.

Etienne a fait parler son talent, il a mis un top but, un lob de près de 50 mètres du gauche alors que c'est un droitier. J'ai bien aimé l'état d'esprit des mecs, même à 2-0 on ne s'est pas relâché, on a continué d'attaquer et surtout de ne pas prendre de but. Cette victoire vient une fois de plus récompenser tout le boulot des joueurs. Vraiment, ça fait plaisir de coacher une vraie équipe, l'état d'esprit de tous les joueurs, notamment celui d'Adam qui a fait un très bon match au milieu. Tout le monde esst concerné, c'est appréciable !".

Feyenoord are facing a heavy fine from European football authorities after fireworks were let off during their Champions League defeat by Internazionale.

Referee Glenn Nyberg suspended the match for several minutes after flares were fired onto the roof from outside De Kuip stadium, damaging the structure. Police later made two arrests.

“It’s obviously not right and it’ll be another fine,” coach Giovanni van Bronckhorst stated wearily after the game, which ended in a comprehensive 3-0 defeat for his team.

According to recent reports, one flare landed on the pitch despite the club taking measures such as hanging nets from the gantries to stop objects being thrown from the stands. “They’re letting off fireworks from outside now,” Van Bronckhorst said. “What do you do about that?”.

Uefa are likely to hit Feyenoord with a fine and could order the club to close parts of the stadium for their next home matches in the competition, against Porto on November 24 and RB Leipzig on January 27.

The club also have a suspended penalty hanging over them from last October, when they were fined €60,000 after fans let off fireworks during the match against Greek club Panathinaikos.

On the pitch, Feyenoord were undone by a classic display of Italian defending and counter-attacking, as Internazionale sat back after taking an eighth-minute lead through Yann Bisseck.

Francesco Pio Esposito headed in a second early in the second half, just as Feyenoord were pushing for an equaliser, before Piotr Zielinski made sure of the win with a shot from 20 metres.

Captain Luciano Valente mentioned the result was “more than deserved” and the visitors had shown more “quality”.

“This defeat was harder to take than the one against Barcelona,” he told Ziggo Sport. “Because we thought going in that we could get something, but we just weren’t good enough.”.

According to recent reports, van Bronckhorst mentioned he was not surprised by the difference in class between the teams. “They scored the first goal out of nothing,” he said. “And Inter know better what the game needs at every stage.

In a recent development, “Their players have a lot of experience, they’ve been in the final twice in the last four years. So we’re at a disadvantage.”.

As part of PortuGOAL’s efforts to constantly evolve and serve lovers of Portuguese football with top-quality and increasingly accessible content, we are replacing the PortuGOAL Android and Apple APPs with a new Progressive Web Application (PWA) as from tomorrow, Tuesday 3 April.

This substantial step forward in phone apps technology loads the content instantly, even in areas of low connectivity, stays up to date at all times, displays the most recent version upon launching, is more efficient than native apps, works on-demand and is always accessible, without taking up a smartphone’s valuable memory or data. This is a football site, not a technology one, but for those of you of a techy nature, click here for more on why PWAs are the future of phone applications.

In another improvement, the website itself will be implementing SSL technology at the same time, leading to more secure and faster navigation. PortuGOAListas should be directed to the new URL automatically from tomorrow, if not simply type http://portugoal.net into your browser’s address bar then bookmark the page. Just a quick detour… now back to the football!

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish

💡 Key Takeaways
  • See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.
  • See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.
  • PSV Eindhoven endured a frustrating night in the Champions League as their defensive frailties were exposed in a 2-1 defeat by Club Brugge.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

PSV Eindhoven endured a frustrating night in the Champions League as their defensive frailties were exposed in a 2-1 defeat by Club Brugge.

PSV started full of attacking intent and should have taken an early lead when Ivan Perisic put Sergiño Dest clean through on goal, but the defender’s shot was too close to goalkeeper Yann Sommer.

Instead it was the visitors who took the lead with their first real attack when Nicolo Tresoldi headed in a teasing cross from Joaquin Seys.

PSV equalised early in the second half as an outstanding pass by Sven Mijnans into the path Lutsharel Geertruida allowed the defender to charge to the byline. His pullback found its way to Kodai Sano, whose shot took a deflection off Seys into the net.

But five minutes later PSV were caught out as another razor-sharp pass by Seys released Carlos Forbs in space to net the winner.

The home side refused to give up, but were unable to find a way past Sommer in the closing stages as the Belgian side closed out the win.

According to recent reports, team captain Mauro Junior admitted that PSV had been undone by shortcomings at the back. “We had a lot of opportunities in the first half but we didn’t score,” he told Ziggo Sport.

“We want to attack and score goals, but we weren’ well organised today in defence. We need to keep our heads up and look forward to the next game.”.

The result leaves PSV in 24th place, just above the elimination line, ahead of their next match away to Real Madrid on November 24, with four points from their opening four matches.

Top five football betting tips and tricks

📅 31 Aug 2018 | ⏱️ 4 min read (785 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Portugoal

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Football is the world’s most famous sport, and it is the sport of choice of a great many sports punters as well.
  • Industry observers note that getting started on football betting is far from easy, though.
  • But experience is not the only thing that can help you become a better football punter.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Football is the world’s most famous sport, and it is the sport of choice of a great many sports punters as well. Especially popular in Europe, betting on football can be an incredibly profitable enterprise, so long as you know how to do it.

Industry observers note that getting started on football betting is far from easy, though. This form of gambling requires dedication, investment, and persistence. As you gain experience, your intuition will improve and you will be able to make more correct predictions.

But experience is not the only thing that can help you become a better football punter. In fact, you can substantially improve your betting strategy by simply following some basic football betting tips.

You might find shopping around boring and unhelpful, but you just have to do it when you search sites for football betting. As you know, the higher the odds, the bigger the payout. What you may have missed, however, is that odds are different at each bookmaker. Having noted that, shopping around for the best odds is sensible, as it rewards you with bigger payouts.

In a recent development, in this line of thought, sticking to one bookmaker is virtually pointless. Even if the bookie of your choosing offers the best odds for a number of matches, it is highly unlikely that their odds will remain the best for long.

An obvious one, we know. And yet, you will be surprised by the number of football bettors who wager on football, but do not follow the sport. So, why is it important to follow the action closely?

First of all, by watching football matches, you can take part in the most exciting football betting market – the live betting market. What is more important, however, is that following the action provides an invaluable insight into teams and players’ style, condition, and determination – important factors  to consider when placing a bet.

Recent findings suggest that as you watch more and more games, you will improve your analytic abilities. In time, you will be able to make more accurate predictions about the outcome of different matches, which, of course,  will result in placing more winning bets.

Industry observers note that as you know, odds are based on the probability of occurrence of a certain outcome; the higher the odds, the more unlikely it is for that outcome to actually occur. But what happens when the odds offered by the bookmaker represent a probability that is lower than the actual probability of an outcome occurring? In such a situation, you can place what is called a value bet.

If you want to become a professional football punter, you should always search for value when betting, as it leads to huge profits.

In a recent development, favoured by beginners in particular, accumulators are a type of football wager which allows you to bet on as many fixtures as you like. Most commonly, you will be asked to choose a match winner, but as the market is diverse, you may be offered a number of other betting options. What makes accumulators an appealing betting market is the huge potential payout – here, you can stake as little as £1 and have the potential to win more than £500,000, depending on the bookmaker and the number of selected fixtures.

Recent findings suggest that if you find accumulators’ payouts too good to be true, you are right. As a matter of fact, there is a reason for the odds to be set so high – actually winning an accumulator bet, especially one which involves a wide selection of matches, is nearly impossible. You see, all you need for your whole wager to lose is one wrong prediction. For example, if you bet on 10 matches and just one of them goes wrong, your entire accumulator is lost.

To make money by betting on football, avoid betting on accumulators – the risk is simply not worth it.

Industry observers note that finally, if you want to be a successful football punter, learn how not to mix emotions with betting. This is easier mentioned than done, though.

Whenever your favourite team plays, you want them to win, regardless of how (im)possible that may be. If you do not learn how to leave emotions out of betting, however, you are highly likely to put money on your favourite team even if they have no chance of winning the match. Conversely, should you base your bets on hard facts and not on emotions, you increase your chances to win.

Our advice – avoid betting on fixtures that involve one of your favourite teams, that is the easiest way to keep emotions at bay.

Pour son 4ème match en ligue 1 tunisienne, l'ancien Vert, Rayan Boukadida (19 ans) a inscrit son 1er but permettant à son club, l'US Monastir de l'emporter (2-0) sur l'Etoile Sportive du Sahel. Ce but, il l'a inscrit, comme souvent avec les équipes de jeunes de l'ASSE, de la tête suite à un coup-franc venu de la gauche. Il permet à l'US Monastir de grimper à la 4ème place, à 2 points du leader.

It has been revealed that rayan Boukadida, un enfant de Sainté, né à Saint-Etienne en 2007 a rejoint l'ASSE en 2013. Il avait 6 ans. Il a fait toute l'Ecole de Foot, toute la préformation chez les Verts. Il est entré au centre de formation en 2022, et n'a pas été conservé en 2025. Il a rejoint les rangs du Mans FC pour la saison 2025-2026, sa seule saison dans la cité mancelle car, le 2 août 2026, l'US Monastir, club de Ligue 1 tunisienne, a annoncé l'arrivée de l'ancien défenseur central vert. Rayan Boukadida rejoint donc un pays qu'il connaît bien puisqu'il compte 16 sélections dans les équipes U17 à U23 de Tunisie, en attendant mieux. Une belle opportunité pour lui certainement.

Le passage de Rayan Boukadida à l'ASSE n'est pas passé inaperçu car ce puissant défenseur central a la particularité d'avoir inscrit 18 buts en 4 saisons (de U15 à U19): - 2021-2022 : 4 buts avec les U15 de Jean-Philippe Primard- 2022-2023 : 3 buts avec les U17 Nationaux de Patrick Moreau- 2023-2024 : 5 buts avec les U17 de Frédéric Dugand- 2024-2025 : 6 buts avec les U19 de Frédéric Dugand.

Pour voir le but de Rayan Boukadida, c'est ici (à 5'25").

Newcastle and Liverpool serve up thrilling tribute to Kevin Keegan

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A last-minute goal, a sense of what might have been and a helter-skelter contest that will take days to decipher.
  • Newcastle versus Liverpool became the Premier League’s most dramatic fixture when Kevin Keegan was manager here and, on the afternoon they flocked to the “cathedral on the hill” to pay tribute to the late, great superstar, we were treated to a contest that was in keeping with his narrative.
  • Liverpool operating with the discipline of a basketball team undoubtedly helped, and we can examine those gaping chasms soon enough, but the poignancy of seeing Matthias Jaissle looking as bereft as Keegan at Anfield 30 years ago at the final whistle was impossible to ignore.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It had to end that way, didn’t it? A last-minute goal, a sense of what might have been and a helter-skelter contest that will take days to decipher.

Newcastle versus Liverpool became the Premier League’s most dramatic fixture when Kevin Keegan was manager here and, on the afternoon they flocked to the “cathedral on the hill” to pay tribute to the late, great superstar, we were treated to a contest that was in keeping with his narrative.

Liverpool operating with the discipline of a basketball team undoubtedly helped, and we can examine those gaping chasms soon enough, but the poignancy of seeing Matthias Jaissle looking as bereft as Keegan at Anfield 30 years ago at the final whistle was impossible to ignore.

Recent findings suggest that really, the German’s first match in charge of Newcastle should have ended with three points. His team are a work in progress – rich in youthful exuberance though prone to lapses – but how they fought, ran and worked to give the locals the result they wanted.

It has been revealed that they were almost at the finish line, seconds away from beating Liverpool here for the first time since December 2015, but then Lewis Hall ran into Victor Muñoz, sending the Spanish substitute sprawling, and Stuart Attwell pointed to the penalty spot. Dominik Szoboszlai inflicted maximum damage.

In a recent development, dominik Szoboszlai equalises from the spot in the 99th minute! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/0Ag9WitqHt.

“I have clear thoughts,” Jaissle said quietly, as he was asked to reflect on the day-wrecking decision. “I guess you call it a soft penalty here. If you give it, you need to give a lot during this match and a lot during the season. I don’t know if it that is good for football.”.

Here was the third time in four seasons Liverpool had scored in injury time in front of the Leazes Stand, after Darwin Núñez (2023) and Rio Ngumoha (2025), and their eighth goal beyond the 90th minute in collisions with Newcastle is a Premier League record against the same opponents.

No wonder he was stunned. Jaissle had spent idle moments in the build-up thinking about what might happen if Newcastle scored an early goal and, much to his delight, fantasy became reality in the most thrilling fashion. On this emotional afternoon, it was fitting the hosts scored first.

One of Keegan’s great early wins as Newcastle manager was in November 1993, when his team blew away Liverpool in the snow and Andy Cole scored a first-half hat-trick. His first goal that day came after five minutes and, by happy coincidence, the clock stopped at that moment for Anthony Elanga, too.

How Liverpool went from having a chance of their own to conceding 20 seconds later is something Andoni Iraola will have to address quickly, but that is what happened: Ryan Gravenberch should have shot, instead he passed and Amar Dedic intervened, his interception finding Will Osula.

Off Osula galloped, Liverpool’s defenders looking leaden-footed as they gave pursuit, and he ushered Elanga into open space. Once he was in the clear, he was not for catching and his shot was perfectly placed beyond Alisson Becker.

It has been revealed that an electric start! Anthony Elanga gives Newcastle the lead inside 5 minutes! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/8DYYFJ9i6F.

As Elanga was mobbed, the recriminations started. Fingers pointed at each other, Iraola spun around in dismay. Liverpool were easy to play against last season – Iraola’s Bournemouth had scored two identical goals against them on the opening day 12 months ago – and old habits die hard.

It has been revealed that “We should finish the play,” Iraola conceded. “We created a great chance. We are on the edge of the box and have a clear opening to shoot and we decide not to. We don’t finish it properly and then you have to give credit to Elanga, who wins the race.”.

What could Liverpool offer in response? The answer before the interval was nothing, other than a shot from Florian Wirtz that was well saved by Lukas Hornicek. The first half was wretched and it was difficult to see what had changed from the final throes of Arne Slot.

Industry observers note that this, to be clear, is no criticism of Iraola, more a spotlight on players who need to step up. They did that momentarily in the second period, when Cody Gakpo equalised. He was afforded too much time by Newcastle’s defence but, still, his finish from 20 yards was super, zipping beyond Hornicek.

Cody Gakpo with a fine finish to equalise for Liverpool! 🎯 pic.twitter.com/cfDQWbES2v.

But parity was secured for less than two minutes before Newcastle scored a near-carbon-copy second goal, another counter-attack – this was one led by the outstanding Yoane Wissa – ending with substitute Joe Willock finding a corner of Alisson’s net. Again the inquests followed.

"Wow!"Joe Willock restores Newcastle's advantage almost instantly with an exceptional finish! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/8IKPUgqapK.

“We had the numbers to defend it better,” Iraola mentioned. “It’s not like they caught us by surprise, but we didn’t defend it properly. We should compete for the first ball and probably make a foul, be a little more aggressive as we had the numbers to defend it.

“You don’t want to concede transitions and we’d been preparing them in the week for transitions.”.

Why they didn’t follow the proposal that had been set is something that Iraola must address, but he will be relieved that the days spent this week are not dissecting a defeat, as Wissa should have wrapped up the contest, only for Alisson to make a brilliant save to thwart the Congolese striker.

Those missed chances should not have mattered but in the final throes, Hall misjudged the angle Muñoz attacked him from, he got his challenge wrong and, after a pause, Attwell pointed to the spot. Given the agony Liverpool have inflicted, the outcome was as clear as black and white.

According to recent reports, “We scored at the end, so you have a better taste,” Iraola said. “Before the game, we wouldn’t have signed for this result. It’s a reward. It’s only a point, but at least it’s something that’s deserved.”.

Plenty would contest his conclusion. Liverpool got away with it – and Iraola is about to find the hard work is only just beginning.

A man who meant so much to both clubs: a phenomenal player for Liverpool and a force of nature who transformed Newcastle as both a player and a manager.

The cooperation between the two to ensure St James’ Park can deliver a special tribute to a remarkable figure in English football has been heartwarming.

Clear communication is at the heart of everything. He explains what he expects, what he needs and what has to be done, no matter who the conversation is with.

It is fitting that Newcastle United vs Liverpool is a Premier League opening weekend fixture following the death of Kevin Keegan at the age of 75 last month.

All corners of St James’ Park will pay tribute and show their appreciation for the former player and manager who means a great deal to both sets of supporters.

Fans will find a printed message from the Keegan family on the back of black and white cards on their seat, which they will hold up to display a mural before kick-off.

As well as playing for both clubs, Keegan was Newcastle’s manager when they were beaten by a last-gasp Stan Collymore goal at Anfield in April 1996, a 4-3 defeat remembered as one of the great Premier League games.

In a recent development, this fixture usually delivers entertainment, and with fresh managers Matthias Jaissle and Andoni Iraola promising front-footed, ‘vertical’ football, there should be goals. That was certainly the case last August, when Newcastle fought back from two down with 10 men, before Rio Ngumoha scored a memorable winner.

Industry observers note that it has been a summer of tumult for Newcastle, losing manager Eddie Howe, as well as key players Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes. There has been bullish talk of “Newcastle 2.0” from David Hopkinson, the club’s chief executive, and the club believe they have found a promising coach, but fans have understandably revised expectations downwards.

According to recent reports, liverpool are a difficult team to read; champions only 18 months ago but brittle last season, which resulted in Arne Slot’s dismissal. Iraola’s appointment is a shift back towards Jurgen Klopp’s style. That will be music to the ears of Anfield regulars, but holes remain in the squad. Central midfield has not been replenished; they need a Mohamed Salah replacement, and their strength at full-back is questionable. Comme le rapporte la dernière édition du Progrès, la préfecture de la Loire a volé hier à la rescousse de celle de la Marne, qui a obligé la veille les supporters stéphanois à rebrousser chemin à quelques encablures du stade Auguste-Delaune, les ayant donc privé d'assister à la victoire des Verts à Reims. Extraits.

It has been revealed that "Ce dimanche, la préfecture de la Loire est entrée dans l'arène pour "rapporter plusieurs précisions". L'autorité représentant l'Etat rappelle que "le Conseil d'Etat a rejeté la demande de suspension des arrêtés du Ministre de l'Intérieur et de la préfecture de la Marne. Dès lors les mesures d'interdiction visant les convois collectifs de supporters demeuraient pleinement exécutoires." Elle conteste l'interprétation qui a été faite de la précision du Conseil d'Etat qui aurait fait "de l'accès individuel au stade sans signe distinctif" une autorisation de "déplacement collectif". Selon la jurisprudence, le simple "fait de se rendre en autocar suffit à caractériser la qualité de supporter." Et donc légitime l'intervention des forces de l'ordre qui "n'ont fait qu'appliquer le droit en vigueur et les arrêtés d'interdiction" en renvoyant les supporters chez eux.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

PSV returned to the top of the Eredivisie with a thumping 5-2 win over Cambuur Leeuwarden as previous leaders Feyenoord lost a seven-goal thriller against the other Frisian club, Heerenveen.

It took just 46 seconds for PSV to get off the mark as Sven Mijnans headed in unmarked.

The midfielder added a second after 15 minutes and completed his hat-trick with a free-kick in the 80th minute to make the score 4-2, just as Cambuur were threatening a comeback.

Industry observers note that feyenoord’s dip in form continued as they let a two-goal lead slip at Heerenveen. The Rotterdammers looked to be in control going into the break with a trademark drilled shot by Anis Hadj Moussa and a penalty by Nacho Ferri.

But Maas Willemsen bundled in the ball from a corner on the stroke of half-time, before Ringo Meerveld came on for the second half and scored a hat-trick as Feyenoord’s defence crumbled under pressure.

“In the matches when we played well I saw a team that fought for each other,” Feyenoord coach Giovanni van Bronckhorst noted after the game. “Mentally strong, kept running even when we didn’t have the ball. That’s our strength. When we don’t do that we’re a lesser team.”.

Mexx Meerdink scored a hotly contested late penalty to settle a tempestuous game in Alkmaar as AZ came back from 3-1 down against Groningen to claim their first win in five matches.

Industry observers note that goalkeeper Etienne Vaessen was given a second yellow card for protesting too hard against the decision to penalise him for upending Ayoub Oufkir. Once the commotion died down Meerdink, who had missed from the spot against Vaessen earlier in the second half, made no mistake against substitute goalkeeper Lovro Stubljar.

Ajax missed the chance to take over top spot at Twente as their former striker Wout Weghorst scored a last-minute penalty to rescue a point for the home side.

Ajax had been 2-0 up with a bullet header by their giant striker Tolu Arokodare and a long-range strike by Rayane Bounida, before an own goal by Dies Janse brought the visitors back into the game.

Fortuna Sittard also had to settle for a point against Telstar after going 2-0 up thanks to a bizarre own goal by Sem Valk. The defender’s sliced clearance looped over the head of Ronald Koeman Junior as the goalkeeper tried to head it away rather than risk being penalised for handling a backpass.

Goals just before half-time by Abdelnour Soualhia and Patrick Brouwer brought Telstar back into the game, but neither side was able to find a winner after the break.

That result allowed ADO, under the guidance of interim coach Levi Schwiebbe, to close the gap on 16th-placed Telstar to one point with a 3-1 win against Sparta, while bottom Willem II collected their third point of the season at home to PEC Zwolle.

ADO Den Haag 3-1 Sparta Rotterdam.

Cambuur Leeuwarden 2-5 PSV Eindhoven.

It has been revealed that depuis janvier 2026, Bilal Benkhedim (25 ans), l'ancien Vert, vainqueur de la Coupe Gambardella 2019, opère dans les rangs du Mouloudia Club d'Oran, club de la Ligue 1 algérienne. Après un début de saison en demi-teinte, il s'installe peu à peu dans son équipe. Après une première entrée en jeu le 30 octobre contre l'Olympique Akbou, il a été titularisé le 4 novembre contre MC Alger, et tout récemment, vendredi dernier, contre la JS Saoura. Lors de ce match remporté 3-1 par le Mouloudia Club d'Oran (désormais 3ème au classement), il a inscrit le 2ème but dans le temps additionnel de la 1ère mi-temps, d'un magnifique tir de l'angle de la surface dans un angle fermé.

Le but de Bilal Benkhedim, c'est ici.

La carrière de Bilal Benkhedim à l'ASSE :.

- 2016-2017 : U17 nationaux avec Jean-Philippe Primard : 20 matchs, 6 buts- 2017-2018 : U17 nationaux avec Razik Nedder : 18 matchs, 23 buts ; U19 nationaux avec Lilian Compan : 2 matchs, 1 but.- 2018-2019 : U19 nationaux avec Razik Nedder : 9 matchs, 7 buts, victoire en Coupe Gambardella ; N2 avec Laurent Batlles : 13 matchs, 3 buts.- 2019-2020 : N2 avec Razik Nedder : 11 matchs, 2 buts ; pro avec Claude Puel : 3 matchs en L1, 1 match en Europa League, 1 match en Coupe de la Ligue, 1 match en Coupe de France.- 2020-2021 : N3 avec Razik Nedder : 1 match, 1 but ; pro avec Claude Puel : L1 : 3 matchs- 2021-2022 : N3 avec Razik Nedder : 8 matchs, 1 but.

Opinion: The morality of football

📅 08 Jun 2023 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1296 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Portugoal

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Yesterday evening, Selecao correspondent Nathan Motz accepted a unique opportunity to appear as a guest on the Moral Maze – a BBC radio broadcast dealing with matters of moral and ethical significance.
  • In a recent development, is football a moral force for good?
  • Nathan’s segment was concerned with whether football has transcendent moral value, and what that is exactly.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Yesterday evening, Selecao correspondent Nathan Motz accepted a unique opportunity to appear as a guest on the Moral Maze – a BBC radio broadcast dealing with matters of moral and ethical significance.

In a recent development, is football a moral force for good? That was the question of the day, and each of the four guests were asked to discuss various aspects of the debate from financial fairplay to club takeovers by foreign entities to racism.

Nathan’s segment was concerned with whether football has transcendent moral value, and what that is exactly. Is there a greater significance to the game we are watching, or is it merely 22 humans kicking a leather ball into a net?

Join Nathan as he elaborates on the most significant takeaways of what was a fascinating discussion on the sport and morality in general.

Football, for some, may be the most poignant reminder of the moral universe in which we live. While debate has raged for centuries regarding the precise origin of moral absolutes and how humans ought to live, it is simply unavoidable to say humanity is often troubled by events surrounding the game we all love so dearly.

It has been revealed that in not so distant history, every normal act of human life would have been assigned some degree of moral significance. Every action had inherently moral indicators - for good or for evil. Today, postmodern views of morality dominate. These describe morality as an entirely subjective dimension. In other words, it cannot be pinned down exactly whether behaviors are objectively good or bad. We can only find fault with someone else’s interpretation based on their own unique moral code. Morality is relative to the individual or society.

It has been revealed that yet last night’s dialogue concerning football and human behavior was filled with moral accusations and claims which strongly suggested humans are not content with relativist morality. Indeed, we are at times frightened by and disgusted with what we observe in and around football. Our sense of moral justice is deeply disturbed. But with respect to what exactly?

Recent findings suggest that in responding to the panelist’s questions, I observed a familiar paradigm. Each time I have discussed any aspect of moral behavior, the speculation humans are good or at worst morally neutral animals continually reemerges. This widely accepted presupposition is then followed shortly by disgust at some aspect of human behavior. Almost as if to ask “why are all these good humans behaving so badly?” while ignoring the very real implications of this line of inquiry. A question rendered unanswerable by the insistent a priori assumptions from which it was derived.

If humans are intrinsically beneficent, conscientious, fair, humble, and honest then why is football rife with racism, misogyny, greed, disenfranchisement, lies, cheating, violence, and the hypocrisy to deny the occurrence of any such behaviors except when a rival club is the guilty party? Behaviors which are perpetrated by individual supporters, fanatical groups, club administrations, corporate bodies such as FIFA, political entities, nations, and even the players themselves. No one participating faction is guiltless.

To so blithely sidestep more sufficient explanations for the empirical reality of wickedness in football and in human behavior more generally is not just factually incorrect. It undermines real attempts to understand the root of these behaviors where they might be dealt with more effectively.

To listen to The Moral Maze episode entitled “Football: a moral force for good?” produced by BBC radio and featuring PortuGOAL’s Seleção correspondent Nathan Motz click on this link.

According to recent reports, furthermore, in good faith, how successful is a response against heinous evil when those perpetrating it are regarded as behaving in accord with their unique moral ambitions? Humans refuse to accept their indisputably objective moral lacking at a fundamental level. This restricts us from ever doing any more than “stamping out” the alleged impropriety of others – while we ourselves may readily engage in these very same behaviors. Moral relativism cannot account for the moral outrage emanating from all corners of the football world. Is Qatar wrong to perpetrate human rights atrocities or is it allowable because their culture is indifferent? Is hooliganism objectively wrong, or only when someone else’s club is responsible?

Recent findings suggest that the overlooking of our own failings while lashing out at others for theirs is quintessential to the morally fallen nature of humanity itself. Football tells all. There are not good people and bad people. There are only people who both willfully and unintentionally transgress the moral code embedded in each of our hearts. A moral law which can only have ever been given by a moral Lawgiver. Otherwise, it is truly your word against mine as it pertains to the moral validity of all behaviors - even those which may deeply violate your conscience.

Football generates an episodic, semantic, and imagistic description of universal archetypes: good and evil, sacrifice and greed, cruelty and mercy, hero and anti-hero. It speaks to every arc of life’s plotline: tragedy, comedy, victory, defeat, the finite nature of our circumstances. It is one of the preeminent existential dialects alongside religion, visual art, written and spoken language, music, and theatre. Football plucks a primal chord.

It has been revealed that as metaphysics have been curtailed to just physics in the modern secular West, football has only elevated our awareness of the often dire moral predicaments of our species. Yet it is clear the moral conversation does not originate on a football pitch. The pitch is but a grand stage upon which moral themes may be observed and critiqued, a mirror held in front of our own soul.

It has been revealed that the desire for ultimate purpose, for meaning beyond the material realm, never disappeared in modernity. Arguably, it has only become more desperate as the outcry for ultimate significance comes under more scrutiny and criticism by those who constrain ontological explanations to those accounted for by physics. The severity of the mental health crisis in the West is in no small part explained by the terrifying existential awareness we are cut adrift in an abstract sea of meaningless, hopeless wandering between two oblivions - that before mortal life began and that at mortal life’s end. Let football be one voice which reassures you - there is ultimate meaning and good reasons why football so unsettles our craving for justice.

In a palpable, unavoidable way, football and supporter communities across Europe are encountering moral quandaries. In Portugal, age-old debates between FC Porto and Benfica have routinely been haunted by, in many cases, farcical and cynical hypocrisy. Throughout its history, the FPF has been susceptible to showing partiality to a club, player, or style which ultimately degrades the performance of our beloved Seleção. Deny it all we like, and not one aspect of this reality is changed.

In conclusion, whatever your thoughts or beliefs on the subject of moral significance, its origin, the meaning of life, and how football draws that out, I hope it will be beneficial to examine these matters more deeply. In my zeal, I admit I have not always been prudent to initiate these discussions in a way which respects thoughtful disagreement. It is my hope this effort to bring that discussion to Portuguese football will be well-received and carefully pondered. But I will contentedly listen to those followers who may be genuinely unhappy or unsupportive of this or any other idea about which I write.

It has been revealed that the readers of this website and the larger Portuguese football loving world are my people. It is a joy and a responsibility I take seriously whenever I have the opportunity to raise important questions about the Selecao, the game, and our lives in general.
